correctness.rationale: A blue cell sees exactly the sum of the white degrees of its two endpoints. This deletes a leaf edge only with an opposite-side isolate; a cycle cannot lose its first edge, and the first permitted deletion creates isolates on both sides. At the white-edge maximum m+n−2 there is one isolated vertex and one spanning tree with an opposite-side leaf. For the final exchange claim, fixed-isolate/fixed-leaf fibers reduce to spanning-tree basis exchange and a freely reattachable leaf. Two chosen leaf fibers meet via a third column or row. The repaired proof constructs trees explicitly to change the isolate within a side, and reconnects across sides by replacing a column leaf edge with an edge at the former row isolate. On the two-column board the apex and omission/addition patterns classify all extremizers. For t≥4 a single exchange cannot switch the dominant column; inside a class the crown line adjacency tests equality of the omitted row or the added row. The apex adds t(t−1) edges to the line graph's t(t−1)(t−2) edges. The explicit switch at t=3 and the four-cycle at t=2 handle the boundary cases. Independent direct forcing and adjacency checks gave component sizes [4], [14], [13,13], [21,21], [72], and [420] on (2,2), (3,2), (4,2), (5,2), (3,3), and (3,4), respectively.
residual_risks: Finite runs corroborate, but the proof, not the finite computations, establishes the all-parameter statement.
